issues.title: validate-references silently strips [bracketed] text from snippets before matching
issues.body: Found while working #496, and it is a separate and more consequential bug than the misleading note that issue is about. ## What happens `Asgard_Wetland_Soil_Methanogenesis_Substrate_Community` carries this snippet, which **is verbatim in its cached full text**: ```yaml snippet: expression of genes for [NiFe]-hydrogenases ``` `just validate-references` reports: ``` [ERROR] Text part not found as substring: 'expression of genes for -hydrogenases' ``` Note the two spaces. **`[NiFe]` has been removed from the snippet before matching**, and the error message quotes the mangled version rather than what the record says. The same happens to `[v/v]` and `[co]`: | record snippet | as matched | |---|---| | `N2:CO2 (80:20 [v/v]) to a final pressure of 172 kPa` | `N2:CO2 (80:20 ) to a final pressure of 172 kPa` | | `50 mL of fresh BG-11[co] medium was added` | `50 mL of fresh BG-11 medium was added` | All three are verbatim quotes. All three fail. ## Why it matters more than the count suggests Only **4** of 5315 snippets currently contain square brackets, and 3 of those are verbatim-and-failing. So the present damage is small. The problem is what brackets *are*: `[NiFe]`, `[v/v]`, `[co]`, `[35S]`, `[Fe-S]` — enzyme cofactors, volume ratios, medium variants, isotopic labels. This bug makes a whole class of precise quotation unusable, and it fails **silently**, in the sense that the failure looks like a bad snippet rather than a tool artefact. It also compounds #496: the accompanying note says *"only abstract available"* for a reference whose full text is cached, so the reader is pointed twice in the wrong direction — once at the cache and once at their own snippet. ## Related, and probably the same root cause The DOI cache `references_cache/DOI_10.1186_s13068-017-0736-x.txt` contains **raw HTML markup** — 17 occurrences of ``: ``` Co-cultures of S. elongatus and R. glutinis were sustained over 1 month ``` `cache_fulltext.py` strips inline tags on the Europe PMC XML path (`_INLINE`), but this file came in through a different route with tags intact. A snippet quoting that text verbatim also fails, and I suspect the validator's tag-stripping is what eats the square brackets too — both look like an over-broad markup filter. ## Scope The stripping is upstream in `linkml-reference-validator`, as with #496. Two things are actionable here: 1. `scripts/annotate_reference_errors.py` (added for #496) can flag the bracket case explicitly, so a curator reading the output is told it is a tool artefact rather than a bad quote. 2. The DOI cache with raw `` tags should be re-fetched or stripped, since a cache that carries markup will keep producing snippets that cannot match. I have trimmed two snippets of mine that contained markup — including `` in a snippet is poor curation regardless of whether it matches — but that is a workaround, not a fix.

issues.title: PR #2102: Computed community membership collapses distinct stocks with the same local strain name
issues.body:
Confirmed during the independent read-only audit of PR #2102, already merged as b0a9df35188b40081a3ba8f354ee3b024f8276ad. Reproduced against current main `61392371875097d7de2efaf34acf59274b361427`. Stable finding key: `pr2102-strain-identity-collision`. Severity: P2.

The unmutated two-record E. coli X control passes native strict validation. Changing one record to Bacillus subtilis X also passes SAME_MEMBERSHIP_AS in both directions. A record containing both species with local name X collapses to the same singleton frozenset as one E. coli X member and also passes. The index discards taxon and culture-collection identity before comparison.

Acceptance:

- Do not establish stock identity solely from normalized local strain_name strings or silently collapse two incompatible member entries into one set element.
- Reject or explicitly mark ambiguous cross-record identities when normalized names collide across incompatible taxa or stocks. Preserve verified existing same-stock comparisons and source-stated relations when identity cannot safely be computed.
- Add native strict positive controls and negative fixtures for different species sharing a local name, two distinct members sharing one local name, and ordinary compatible equivalent designation formatting. schema_pr.title: Add host, soil, and related-communities schema and records
schema_pr.body:
## Summary

Adds three things the schema could not express, and tests them on real records from a new paper (Ding et al. 2026, *Nat Commun*, PMID:42660928).

**Schema** (all additive and optional; no existing record needs migrating):
- `related_communities`: links between records (same strains, subset/superset, overlapping, derived from, same study). Field names follow mech_shared `CrossCorpusLink`; each link has a `relation` and a `basis` (`SHARED_STRAIN_DESIGNATIONS` or `SOURCE_STATEMENT`).
- `host`: NCBITaxon (Eukaryota only), host lines as the source names them, PO/UBERON anatomical site and stage, and microbial status. A host is never a `taxonomy` member (#319).
- `soils`: ENVO soil and texture classes, location, and measured values as `Quantity` with UO units (sieve size, pH, water content, organic carbon), plus sterilization.
- `EcologicalInteraction.host_participation` and `effect_direction`.
- New cultivation systems: `PLANT_POT`, `SOIL_MICROCOSM`, `HYDROPONIC_VESSEL`, `FABRICATED_ECOSYSTEM_DEVICE` (staged in `vocab/cultivation_terms.yaml`).
- PO and UO registered with the id↔label gate and ontology adapters (`conf/id_label_targets.yaml`, `conf/oak_config.yaml`, `scripts/ontology_preflight.py`, `OBO_DATABASES`).

The design follows DisMech/mechmaker conventions: one descriptor per role, `term` bound to a dynamic enum whose root was checked in OLS4, `Quantity` with UO units, and verbatim-quote evidence. Section purposes, roots and population rules: `docs/HOST_SOIL_AND_RELATED_COMMUNITIES.md`.

**Checks**
- New `communitymech.validators.related_communities`, wired into `validate-strict`. When both records list a strain for every member, it recomputes membership relations from the strain lists and fails on a mismatch. It also checks that targets exist, rejects self-links and duplicates, requires quotes for `SOURCE_STATEMENT`, fails a host listed as a member, and fails `host_participation` without a `host`. After review (ba65d258) it also fails a link with no inverse link on the target (`related_community_missing_inverse`) and a record id shared by two records (`duplicate_record_id`).
- `linkml-term-validator` rejects wrong-branch terms. Mutated copies with a bacterium as host, a GO process as anatomy, a bioreactor as soil and a soil as unit were each rejected; the unmutated controls passed.
- `tests/test_related_communities.py`, including a mutation test with a control arm.

**Records**
- **CommunityMech:000516** (new): the dopamine paper's hydroponic SynCom16 on ten *Brachypodium* lines, with host, links, and signed host-exudate interactions.
- **CommunityMech:000515** (new): the same paper's dopamine-amended Yolo silt loam microcosm, with `soils`.
- **000025** (ring trial): host Bd21-3, plus links.
- **000087** (Coker et al. SynCom16): links. Its links are quoted rather than computed because it has no strain list yet (#1548).

The two new records were renumbered four times while this PR was open, because `main` minted the same IDs (000496 in #2087; 000497–000498 in #2098; 000505–000506 in #2116; 000510–000511 in #2328). Each renumbering added a curation event and a correction history record; earlier history files are unchanged.

The strain comparison found that the dopamine study's 16 strains differ from Coker et al.'s final 16 by one strain (OAE603 instead of Bradyrhizobium OAE829). The link is recorded as `OVERLAPPING_MEMBERSHIP`, not "same SynCom".

A successor review ledger (`reports/causal_graph_review/decisions/20261029-host-soil-related-communities-paper-test.yaml`) records the non-graph additions to 000025 and 000087. The batch36/batch61 hash tests follow it, the same way batch101 follows its successors.

Review findings #2425–#2428 were addressed in ba65d258 (renumbering, inverse/duplicate checks, schema doc and host template fixes).

## Validation
- `validate-strict` on the whole corpus after the merge before ba65d258: 0 errors.
- `validate-references` on the four edited records: clean. `validate-terms` on all four and `validate-gtdb` on the soil record: clean before the renumberings, which changed no ontology terms.
- `validate-products` (id↔label gate) with the KGX export built: all pairs correspond, including the new PO and UO terms.
- `check-docs-current`: clean. History records validate.
- CI on ba65d258: see the checks on this PR.

## Not included
- Named treatment arms that abundances and interactions can refer to.
- An ontology term on `EnvironmentalFactor`.
- KGX export of the new sections.
- A strain list for 000087 (#1548).
